brief.ask: Create a brand identity for Portwise, the freight visibility platform in this folder.
brief.owner: Owner preferences: dependable and calm, for operations teams who look at it all day; serious enough for enterprise procurement. No globes, ships, containers, trucks or arrows. Web app, sales decks and LinkedIn.

claim.notes: The critic gave 'none' to all three directions (waypoints, tolerance, quay-p) in two sketch-review rounds, so no concept reached the gate and no assets were finalized, exported or installed.

concepts.title: Quay P
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s6 a frying pan / magnifier / power-off button in a square; s7 a plain geometric P in a stock font, nothing of a quay; s8 the brick-wall icon the brief bans (also a firewall icon - wrong for a visibility product); s9 a letter M in a rounded square (an M-initial app icon). The designer's s8 claim is rejected. Different move: keep the P only if the harbour reads first. Build the P bowl as the basin itself: a single heavy L-shaped quay (stem + top) and a mole that closes the bowl but leaves a narrow harbour mouth on the right-lower side, with a counter that is a calm rectangle of water, not a circle. Test against plain P and a 'parking' sign at 16 px; if it reads as parking P, strike.

concepts.title: Tolerance
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s6 a staircase in a rounded square (app-icon cliché, stockShape 0.79); s7 a traffic cone / bell, unfortunate for a freight brand (road works, delay); s8 a bracket pair [ ] offset, the exact shape the brief bans, the offset does not rescue it; s9 three staircases / a stepped chart, banned staircase again. The designer's s8 claim is rejected. Different move: abandon jaws, brackets and steps entirely. Tolerance as a band of certainty: one solid mass whose two edges are not parallel (a narrow-to-wide lozenge or wedge of a single weight) with one fixed notch marking the committed ETA. Or drop the concept if the next pass returns another bracket/stair.

concepts.title: Waypoints
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s6 a window/copy UI icon with an orange tab (or a price tag); s7 Greek-key meander / square spiral, a stock ornament; s8 a split pill sliced and offset, the banned cut device, also a pause/D initial; s9 a step-function / single stair, the brief's banned staircase. None carries 'waypoints'. Different move: stop drawing a line that changes level. Draw the waypoints themselves as the form: e.g. a closed counter-shape built from a fixed number of evenly spaced, identical solid stations (not dots on a path) whose spacing implies the route, with one station in accent where the shipment is now. Must not read as a loading spinner, dice face or progress bar; test at 16 px first.
